newsitem.title: USA: U.S. light foreign crudes scarce amid firm demand.
newsitem.headline: U.S. light foreign crudes scarce amid firm demand.

text.p: U.S.-bound light, sweet crudes from the North Sea and West Africa stayed scarce amid buoyant refiner demand, driving alternative local crudes higher.
A major was seen fixing a 290,000 tonne VLCC on subjects for the U.S. Gulf Coast for Nov 8, but traders said economics were prohibitive and doubted Brent could head west.
"Shell could move the cargoes into their own U.S. system but it doesn't work," an East Coast trader said, adding Brent was valued at Dec West Texas Intermediate plus 90 cents cif.
The Dec West Texas Intermediate/Brent spread at 75-80 cents a barrel was deemed too narrow to attract buyers.
The high cost of sweet imports drove Louisiana Light Sweet/St James to WTI plus 78 cents a barrel, and Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire to WTI plus 88 cents.
Some Nigerian Qua Iboe and Brass River were thought available for November, but firm offers were not seen.
Nearby waterborne trade was mostly thin, with Mexican port closures due to bad weather likely to delay some imports.
In the U.S. after market, Brent paper was briskly traded at slightly lower levels against London's IPE closes.
Dec Brent partials traded four times between $24.15 and $24.05 a barrel, bought by one Wall Street firm.
Brent intermonth Nov/Dec spreads moved twice at 35 cents, once at 33 cents and twice at 32 cents.
